text: As the Patriots prepare to host the Steelers for their home opener on Sunday, September 20 at 1 PM ET, they're facing a significant challenge with wide receiver A.J. Brown heading to injured reserve with a high ankle sprain suffered in Week 1, sidelining him for at least four weeks—a blow that Mike Reiss and others are analyzing in terms of who steps up in his absence during the crucial early stretch of the season. Head Coach Mike Vrabel addressed the team's situation during his Wednesday press conference, and beat writers are focused on whether Drake Maye can lead a bounce-back performance against Pittsburgh after the Week 1 setback. On a lighter note, Maye and his wife Ann Michael demonstrated the kind of character the organization values by funding Amazon classroom wish lists for over 50 teachers and support specialists at Alfred Lima Sr. Elementary School in Providence, Rhode Island, a generous back-to-school donation that showed the quarterback's investment in the community beyond the field. Separately, Patriots owner Robert Kraft made headlines by confirming he had Macklemore removed as an opening act for Ed Sheeran's upcoming Gillette Stadium shows, citing the artist's "history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community."
